item.title: Australian lawmaker has both legs amputated after allegedly deliberate attack by car rammer
item.description:
Independent member for Indi Helen Haines during a press conference in the Mural Hall at Parliament House on June 11, 2020 in Canberra, Australia.
Sam Mooy/Getty Images

Brisbane, Australia —
The Australian lawmaker hit by a car in an allegedly deliberate attack has now had both her legs amputated, her husband announced Wednesday.
Helen Haines, an independent federal MP, remains in a stable condition in hospital after Monday’s incident, which unfolded mid-afternoon on a main road outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, northeastern Victoria.
“Helen’s left leg was amputated on Monday. We had been hoping that her right leg would be saved, but… the surgeons had to also remove her right leg,” Phil Haines, the MP’s husband of nearly 40 years, told a press conference at The Alfred hospital in Melbourne.
“Both her heart and her mind are in good shape,” he added.

item.title: Australian MP Helen Haines critically injured after attack by car
item.description:
Australian independent member of Parliament Helen Haines speaks to journalists at Parliament House in Canberra, Australia, on September 8.
Mick Tsikas/AAP Image/AP
Facebook
Tweet
Email
Link
Threads
Link Copied!
Brisbane, Australia —
A 43-year-old man has been charged with ramming an Australian lawmaker with a vehicle in what police said was a “targeted” attack that inflicted serious injuries requiring the amputation of her leg, according to media reports.
Helen Haines, 65, who represents the federal seat of Indi, was struck by a Toyota four-wheel-drive Land Cruiser in the rural city of Wangaratta at about 3:30 p.m. local time on Monday. The attack generated nationwide debate about the driver’s motives and the safety of Australia’s politicians.
Police have not confirmed the suspect’s name, nor his motive, but local media have identified him as Brendan Nugent.
